explanation:
[EFFECT] The month of the year has a strongly non-monotonic, arch-shaped effect on predicted hourly demand. In January (month 1) the model sharply suppresses demand — contributions are the most negative of any month, around –0.4 to –0.7 in log space, roughly halving or worse the predicted count. Contributions rise steadily through spring, crossing into positive territory around April, and reach their peak boost during the summer and early fall months (roughly June through October), where they add up to +0.1 to +0.25 in log space. December then pulls demand back down, again into negative territory.

[IMPORTANCE] Month is the 5th most important feature out of 9, with an importance score of 0.118. It is meaningfully less influential than the top four features — hour of day (0.833), year (0.200), temperature (0.197), and weekday (0.173) — but still stronger than humidity, weather situation, wind speed, and holiday.

[RECOMMENDATION] Bike availability and staffing should be scaled up significantly from late spring through early autumn (May–October) and scaled down in winter months, particularly January and February, when the model expects materially lower demand regardless of the hour or day of the week.
